disclaimer: Scores and pay ranges are informed estimates for the Indian (Hyderabad/Bengaluru GCC and product-company) and US markets as of late 2026, not live data. Treat them as a starting point and check against current job posts, levels.fyi and recruiter conversations before deciding.

roadmaps.title: AI Platform Engineer (JVM)
roadmaps.tagline: Build the production systems that put LLMs and agents to work inside enterprises.
roadmaps.whyNow: Every enterprise with a Java estate is wiring LLMs into it. Data scientists can build a demo; few people can make agents reliable, secure, observable and cheap at scale on Spring. That gap is exactly your 16 years.

stations.name: Java Microservices Junction
stations.summary: 16+ years of Spring, Kafka and distributed systems. This is your boarding platform.
topics: Audit your current Spring Boot version and move a service to Boot 4 / Java 25
List three internal processes at work an LLM could improve
stations.milestone: Write a one-page note on where AI could plug into your current system.

stations.name: LLM Foundations
stations.summary: Know how the engine works before you drive it.
topics: Tokens, context windows, temperature and sampling
Prompting patterns: few-shot, chain-of-thought, structured output
Model families and trade-offs: frontier vs open-weight vs small
Cost and latency maths per request
Hallucination: why it happens and how to contain it
stations.milestone: A CLI that calls two different model APIs and compares cost, latency and answer quality on 20 prompts.

stations.name: Spring AI & LangChain4j
stations.summary: Your home framework now speaks LLM.
topics: Spring AI ChatClient, advisors and structured output to records
LangChain4j AI Services as a comparison
Streaming responses with WebFlux / SSE
Prompt templates and versioning
Retries, timeouts and fallbacks with Resilience4j
stations.milestone: A Spring Boot service that turns free-text support tickets into typed JSON and pushes them to Kafka.

stations.name: RAG Central
stations.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation is the most deployed enterprise AI pattern. Master it.
topics: Embeddings and similarity search
Vector stores: pgvector, Oracle 23ai Vector Search, MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
Chunking strategies and metadata filtering
Hybrid search (BM25 + vectors) and re-ranking
Ingestion pipelines fed by Kafka / CDC
Citations and access control on retrieved documents
stations.milestone: A RAG service over your team's Confluence/runbooks with citations, permission filtering and Kafka-driven reindexing.

stations.name: Agents & MCP
stations.summary: From chatbots to systems that take actions.
topics: Tool/function calling and its failure modes
Model Context Protocol: build MCP servers in Java
Agent loops, planning and human-in-the-loop approvals
Multi-agent orchestration and when not to use it
Idempotency and sagas when an agent calls your microservices
stations.milestone: An MCP server exposing three of your existing microservice APIs, used by an agent that needs approval before any write.

stations.name: Evals & Guardrails
stations.summary: Testing is where your Karate/JUnit discipline becomes rare and valuable.
topics: Golden datasets and regression evals in CI
LLM-as-judge and its biases
Prompt-injection and data-leak defences
PII redaction and output validation
Running evals as a Harness pipeline gate
stations.milestone: An eval suite of 100+ cases that blocks a Harness deploy when answer quality drops.

stations.name: LLMOps & Cost Control
stations.summary: Production AI is an operations problem.
topics: Tracing with OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions
Semantic caching and prompt caching
Model routing: cheap model first, escalate when needed
Rate limits, quotas and per-tenant budgets
Self-hosting open-weight models on Kubernetes (vLLM) via Helm
stations.milestone: A dashboard showing cost, latency and quality per feature, with a router that cuts spend by 40%.

stations.name: AI Platform Architect
stations.summary: You own the paved road every team uses to ship AI features safely.
topics: Design an internal AI gateway (auth, routing, logging, guardrails)
Write the reference architecture and ADRs
Talk publicly: one blog post or meetup talk on Java + AI in production
stations.milestone: Lead an AI feature from idea to production at work and present the architecture to leadership.

roadmaps.title: Principal Distributed Systems Architect
roadmaps.tagline: Be the person who designs event-driven systems that do not fall over at 10x scale.
roadmaps.whyNow: AI can generate a microservice; it cannot own the trade-offs of consistency, failure and cost across 200 of them. Staff+ architects who have actually run Kafka at scale are scarce, and your experience is the hard-to-copy part.

stations.name: Java Microservices Junction
stations.summary: You already design services. Now design the system of systems.
topics: Draw the current architecture of your product end to end
List the three worst incidents you have seen and their root causes
stations.milestone: An honest C4 diagram of your current system with its weak points marked.

stations.name: Distributed Systems Theory
stations.summary: The theory that makes your intuition explainable.
topics: Designing Data-Intensive Applications (Kleppmann), cover to cover
CAP, PACELC and consistency models (linearizable to eventual)
Clocks, ordering, vector clocks and hybrid logical clocks
Consensus: Raft and how KRaft uses it
Failure modes: partial failure, split brain, gray failure
stations.milestone: Explain to a junior, in writing, why exactly-once in Kafka is really effectively-once.

stations.name: Kafka Deep Dive
stations.summary: Go from user to expert of your strongest tool.
topics: Partitioning strategy, keys and hot partitions
Transactions, idempotent producers and EOS
KRaft, tiered storage and cluster sizing
Schema Registry, Avro/Protobuf and compatibility rules
Kafka Streams state stores and interactive queries
stations.milestone: A load test that pushes a 3-broker cluster to failure, with a written capacity plan.

stations.name: Event-Driven Patterns
stations.summary: The patterns that keep data consistent without distributed transactions.
topics: Event sourcing and CQRS: when they pay off and when they hurt
Transactional outbox with Debezium
Sagas: choreography vs orchestration (Temporal)
Idempotency keys and deduplication
Event versioning and contract testing
stations.milestone: An order-payment-shipping flow using outbox + saga, with chaos tests proving no lost or double orders.

stations.name: Resilience & Multi-Region
stations.summary: Design for the day a region disappears.
topics: Cell-based architecture and blast radius
Active-active vs active-passive, MirrorMaker 2 / Cluster Linking
Back-pressure, load shedding and bulkheads
SLOs, error budgets and graceful degradation
Chaos engineering game days
stations.milestone: A multi-region design doc with RTO/RPO numbers and a failover runbook.

stations.name: Architecture Leadership
stations.summary: At Principal level, writing and influence matter as much as design.
topics: Architecture Decision Records and RFC process
Running design reviews that people want to attend
Cost and FinOps as a design input
Build vs buy vs open-source evaluations
Mentoring senior engineers into tech leads
stations.milestone: Drive one cross-team RFC to an accepted decision.

stations.name: System Design Interviews
stations.summary: Package your experience for Staff+ loops.
topics: Practice 15 classic designs aloud (payments, feeds, rate limiter, chat)
Build stories of your past decisions using STAR
Behavioural loops for Staff+: scope, ambiguity, influence
stations.milestone: Three mock interviews with Staff+ engineers, with feedback recorded.

stations.name: Principal Architect
stations.summary: You are the technical conscience of a large engineering organisation.
topics: Own the long-range technical strategy for a domain
Publish externally: talk, blog or open-source contribution
stations.milestone: A Principal/Staff offer or internal promotion.

roadmaps.title: Platform Engineering Lead
roadmaps.tagline: Build the internal developer platform that makes 500 engineers fast and safe.
roadmaps.whyNow: Companies are consolidating DevOps chaos into platform teams with golden paths. You already ship with Helm and Harness; adding Kubernetes depth, GitOps and platform-as-product thinking makes you a natural lead.
leverage: Microservices → understand what app teams need

stations.name: Java Microservices Junction
stations.summary: You have been a platform customer. Now become its builder.
topics: Measure your team's lead time and deploy frequency (DORA)
List the five biggest friction points developers hit
stations.milestone: A friction log from your own team.

stations.name: Kubernetes Core
stations.summary: Deep, not just kubectl apply.
topics: Pods, controllers, scheduling, requests/limits
Networking: Services, Ingress/Gateway API, CNI
Storage, StatefulSets and operators
RBAC and security contexts
CKA certification
stations.milestone: Pass the CKA and run a JVM service with proper probes, HPA and PodDisruptionBudgets.

stations.name: Infrastructure as Code
stations.summary: Everything versioned, everything reviewable.
topics: Terraform / OpenTofu modules and state
Crossplane for cloud resources via Kubernetes
One cloud deeply: AWS or Azure (associate cert)
Policy as code with OPA / Kyverno
stations.milestone: Terraform modules that create a full environment (cluster, DB, Kafka) from one pull request.

stations.name: GitOps & Delivery
stations.summary: From pipelines you use to pipelines you design for everyone.
topics: Argo CD / Flux and the GitOps model
Progressive delivery: Argo Rollouts, canary, feature flags
Harness templates and pipeline governance at org scale
Helm chart libraries and versioning strategy
stations.milestone: A reusable pipeline template with canary analysis that any service adopts in under an hour.

stations.name: Developer Portal
stations.summary: The platform as a product, with a front door.
topics: Backstage: catalog, templates, TechDocs
Golden paths: Spring Boot service template with everything wired
Scorecards for production readiness
Measuring developer experience (SPACE, DX surveys)
stations.milestone: A Backstage template that creates a production-ready Spring Boot service with CI, Helm chart and dashboards.

stations.name: Observability & SRE
stations.summary: If you cannot see it, you cannot run it.
topics: OpenTelemetry for JVM: traces, metrics, logs
Prometheus, Grafana, Loki/Tempo
SLOs and alerting that respect sleep
Incident management and blameless postmortems
stations.milestone: Default dashboards and SLO alerts that every new service gets automatically.

stations.name: AI for Platforms
stations.summary: Keep the platform ahead of AI, not replaced by it.
topics: AI-assisted incident triage and runbooks
Platform support for AI workloads: GPUs, model serving
Coding agents in the paved road, with guardrails
stations.milestone: An assistant that answers 'why did my deploy fail?' from pipeline logs.

stations.name: Platform Engineering Lead
stations.summary: You run the platform team and its roadmap.
topics: Platform roadmap driven by developer feedback
Adoption metrics and internal marketing
stations.milestone: Lead or found a platform team; show a measurable DORA improvement.

roadmaps.title: Real-Time Data & Streaming Engineer
roadmaps.tagline: Turn your Kafka skills into the real-time data backbone that AI products need.
roadmaps.whyNow: AI features are only as good as fresh data. Firms are moving from nightly batch to streaming with Flink and lakehouses. Kafka experts who also understand data modelling are in short supply.

stations.name: Java Microservices Junction
stations.summary: Your Kafka experience is a ticket most data engineers do not have.
topics: Map every Kafka topic in your system and who consumes it
Note which reports or features still run on nightly batch
stations.milestone: A list of three batch jobs that should be real time.

stations.name: Kafka Streams & ksqlDB
stations.summary: Process in the stream, not after it.
topics: KStream vs KTable, joins and windowing
State stores and changelog topics
Exactly-once processing
Testing with TopologyTestDriver
stations.milestone: A real-time fraud-score stream joining payments with customer profiles.

stations.name: Apache Flink
stations.summary: The engine that has become the standard for stateful streaming.
topics: DataStream API in Java
Event time, watermarks and late data
Checkpoints, savepoints and state backends
Flink SQL and the Table API
Running Flink on Kubernetes with the operator
stations.milestone: A Flink job computing per-minute metrics from Kafka with correct handling of late events.

stations.name: CDC & Integration
stations.summary: Unlock data trapped in Oracle and MongoDB.
topics: Debezium for Oracle (LogMiner) and MongoDB
Kafka Connect: sinks, sources, SMTs
Schema evolution in pipelines
Handling snapshots and backfills
stations.milestone: Stream Oracle table changes into a search index with under 5 seconds of lag.

stations.name: Lakehouse
stations.summary: Streaming meets analytics.
topics: Apache Iceberg tables, snapshots and time travel
Writing Iceberg from Flink / Kafka (Tableflow-style)
Query engines: Trino, Spark SQL
Data modelling: star schema, data vault, medallion layers
stations.milestone: A pipeline from Kafka to Iceberg queried by Trino, with a dashboard on top.

stations.name: Data for AI
stations.summary: The fresh-data supply chain for ML and LLM features.
topics: Feature stores and online/offline consistency
Streaming embeddings into vector stores
Data contracts and quality checks
Lineage and governance (OpenLineage)
stations.milestone: A streaming pipeline that keeps a RAG index fresh within a minute of source changes.

stations.name: Streaming Platform Architect
stations.summary: You own the company's real-time data platform.
topics: Multi-tenant Kafka/Flink platform design
Cost and retention strategy
Confluent or Databricks certification as a signal
stations.milestone: Lead a batch-to-streaming migration that a business team relies on.

roadmaps.title: Legacy Modernization Architect
roadmaps.tagline: Lead banks and enterprises off decades-old systems, with AI agents doing the heavy lifting.
roadmaps.whyNow: Hyderabad's GCCs hold huge Java 8, Oracle and mainframe estates. AI coding agents make large migrations affordable for the first time, but someone who knows both old and new must direct them, check the results and manage risk. Domain plus legacy knowledge is very hard to replace.

stations.name: Java Microservices Junction
stations.summary: You have lived through monolith-to-microservices. That story is worth money.
topics: Write down a migration you were part of: what worked, what failed
Pick a business domain to specialise in (banking, insurance, retail)
stations.milestone: A two-page case study of a past migration.

stations.name: Domain-Driven Design
stations.summary: Find the right seams before you cut.
topics: Bounded contexts and context mapping
Event storming workshops
Aggregates and invariants
Team Topologies and Conway's law
stations.milestone: Run an event-storming session on a real legacy module.

stations.name: Migration Patterns
stations.summary: Change the plane's engines in flight.
topics: Strangler fig and branch by abstraction
Anti-corruption layers
Parallel run and dark launching
Database decomposition: shared DB to owned data
Oracle to PostgreSQL migration techniques
stations.milestone: A strangler-fig plan with phases, rollback points and data sync strategy.

stations.name: Automated Refactoring
stations.summary: Recipes that upgrade a thousand repos at once.
topics: OpenRewrite recipes: Java 8 → 21/25, Spring Boot 2 → 4
Writing custom OpenRewrite recipes
Jakarta EE namespace migrations
Characterisation tests before touching legacy code
stations.milestone: Upgrade a real legacy service to Java 25 / Boot 4 with OpenRewrite and a green test suite.

stations.name: AI-Assisted Migration
stations.summary: Direct coding agents across a whole codebase, safely.
topics: Coding agents for large refactors: planning, batching, verification
Generating tests for untested legacy code
Understanding legacy code with AI: COBOL/PL-SQL explanation
Review workflows and guardrails for AI-written changes
Measuring migration velocity and defect rate
stations.milestone: Migrate a module with AI agents and publish before/after metrics on effort and defects.

stations.name: Business & Risk
stations.summary: Modernization is sold to CFOs, not engineers.
topics: Business cases: cost of delay, TCO, risk reduction
Regulatory concerns (RBI, PCI-DSS, data residency)
Stakeholder management and steering committees
Vendor and partner evaluation
stations.milestone: A business case deck for a modernization programme.

stations.name: Modernization Architect
stations.summary: You lead multi-year programmes with real budgets.
topics: Build a repeatable modernization playbook
Speak at an industry event on AI-assisted migration
stations.milestone: Lead a modernization programme or join a GCC/consultancy as its modernization lead.

roadmaps.title: Application Security & DevSecOps Architect
roadmaps.tagline: Secure Java systems, software supply chains and the new attack surface AI opens.
roadmaps.whyNow: Supply-chain attacks, stricter regulation and AI agents with access to production have made security a board-level concern. Security engineers who can actually read and fix Java code are rare, and accountability for security cannot be handed to a model.

stations.name: Java Microservices Junction
stations.summary: Builders make the best defenders.
topics: Run a dependency scan on your main service and read the report
List where secrets live in your current setup
stations.milestone: A security debt list for your own system.

stations.name: Secure Coding & OWASP
stations.summary: Learn how attackers think about your code.
topics: OWASP Top 10 and API Security Top 10
Injection, SSRF, deserialization in Java
Hands-on labs: PortSwigger Web Security Academy
Secure code review checklists
stations.milestone: Find and fix five real vulnerabilities in a deliberately vulnerable Spring app.

stations.name: Identity & Zero Trust
stations.summary: Who is calling, and should they be?
topics: OAuth 2.1, OIDC, PKCE, token exchange
Spring Authorization Server and Spring Security 7
mTLS and service mesh identity (SPIFFE)
Fine-grained authorisation: OPA, Cedar, ReBAC
stations.milestone: Service-to-service auth with mTLS plus fine-grained authorisation across three services.

stations.name: Supply Chain Security
stations.summary: Your Maven dependencies are an attack surface.
topics: SBOMs (CycloneDX) and vulnerability management
Sigstore signing, SLSA levels and provenance
Container image hardening and scanning
Secrets management: Vault, external secrets
stations.milestone: A Harness pipeline that signs images, produces SBOMs and blocks critical CVEs.

stations.name: Threat Modelling
stations.summary: Find the design flaws scanners never will.
topics: STRIDE and attack trees
Data-flow diagrams for microservices
Risk rating and prioritisation
Security architecture reviews
stations.milestone: Threat model a payment flow and present mitigations to the team.

stations.name: AI Security
stations.summary: The fastest-growing niche in security.
topics: OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications
Prompt injection, data exfiltration via tools, excessive agency
Securing MCP servers and agent permissions
Red-teaming LLM features
stations.milestone: Red-team an internal LLM feature and write the findings report.

stations.name: Certifications
stations.summary: Signals that open security doors.
topics: CSSLP or OSWE (application focus)
CKS for Kubernetes security
Cloud security specialty (AWS/Azure)
stations.milestone: One security certification earned.

stations.name: AppSec Architect
stations.summary: You set the security bar for engineering.
topics: Run a security champions programme
Own secure-by-default templates for all services
stations.milestone: Move into an AppSec/DevSecOps lead role.

roadmaps.title: JVM Performance & Reliability Engineer
roadmaps.tagline: The specialist teams call when latency, GC pauses or cloud bills get out of hand.
roadmaps.whyNow: Cloud cost pressure and low-latency AI serving put performance back in focus. Deep JVM knowledge is niche, hard to learn quickly and much harder to automate than writing CRUD services.

stations.name: Java Microservices Junction
stations.summary: Every slow incident you fixed was training for this.
topics: Find the slowest endpoint in your system and its p99
Check your services' GC logs and heap settings
stations.milestone: A baseline latency and cost report for one service.

stations.name: JVM Internals
stations.summary: Know what the JVM does with your code.
topics: JIT compilation, inlining and escape analysis
Garbage collectors: G1, ZGC (generational), Shenandoah
Memory model, happens-before and safe publication
Class loading and startup: CDS, AOT cache (Project Leyden)
stations.milestone: Cut p99 latency of a service by tuning the GC and explain why it worked.

stations.name: Modern Concurrency
stations.summary: Java 21–25 changed the concurrency game.
topics: Virtual threads and pinning
Structured concurrency and scoped values
Reactive vs virtual threads: when each wins
Lock contention analysis
stations.milestone: Migrate a thread-pool service to virtual threads and benchmark before and after.

stations.name: Profiling & Benchmarking
stations.summary: Measure, do not guess.
topics: JFR and JDK Mission Control
async-profiler and flame graphs
JMH micro-benchmarks done correctly
Load testing with Gatling / k6
stations.milestone: A performance regression test that runs in CI.

stations.name: Native & Startup
stations.summary: Fast startup and small footprints for cloud and serverless.
topics: GraalVM native image with Spring Boot
CRaC checkpoint/restore
Container memory sizing for the JVM
stations.milestone: A native-image build that cuts memory by 60% with a written trade-off analysis.

stations.name: SRE & FinOps
stations.summary: Reliability and cost as engineering disciplines.
topics: SLOs, error budgets and capacity planning
Linux performance: CPU, memory, I/O, eBPF tools
Kubernetes right-sizing and autoscaling
Cloud cost attribution and optimisation
stations.milestone: Save a measurable amount of cloud spend at work and document it.

stations.name: Performance Architect
stations.summary: The person whose name comes up when something is slow.
topics: Build a performance engineering practice
Write publicly about JVM tuning case studies
stations.milestone: Own performance for a critical platform.

roadmaps.title: Engineering Manager → Director
roadmaps.tagline: Multiply impact through people, with AI-augmented teams.
roadmaps.whyNow: As AI makes individual coding cheaper, leaders who can reshape teams, judge quality and own outcomes become more valuable. Senior engineers with deep technical credibility make the most trusted managers in GCCs.

stations.name: Java Microservices Junction
stations.summary: Decide deliberately: manager track or Staff+ IC track. Both are good.
topics: Read 'The Manager's Path' (Fournier)
Talk to two EMs and two Principal engineers about their week
stations.milestone: A written decision on IC vs manager, with reasons.

stations.name: Tech Lead
stations.summary: Lead the work before you lead the people.
topics: Planning and estimation for a team
Running stand-ups, retros and design reviews
Delegation without losing quality
Unblocking others as your main job
stations.milestone: Lead a quarter-long project as tech lead.

stations.name: People Management
stations.summary: The core of the job.
topics: 1:1s that matter
Feedback models (SBI) and difficult conversations
Performance reviews and promotions
Hiring: structured interviews and calibration
stations.milestone: Manage 4–6 engineers with regular 1:1s and a growth plan for each.

stations.name: Delivery & Metrics
stations.summary: Outcomes over output.
topics: DORA and SPACE metrics
OKRs and roadmap planning
Risk management and dependency tracking
Stakeholder communication with product and business
stations.milestone: A quarterly plan with OKRs that your team hits.

stations.name: AI-Augmented Teams
stations.summary: Redesign how your team works with AI tools.
topics: Rolling out coding agents with quality guardrails
Changing review and testing practices for AI-written code
Reskilling plans for the team
Measuring productivity honestly
stations.milestone: An AI adoption plan with before/after delivery metrics.

stations.name: Org Leadership
stations.summary: Managing managers.
topics: Org design and team topologies
Budget and headcount planning
Building culture and retaining talent
Executive communication
stations.milestone: Lead a group of 2–4 teams.

stations.name: Director of Engineering
stations.summary: You own a business area's engineering.
topics: Engineering strategy tied to business goals
Build a leadership bench beneath you
stations.milestone: Director role at a GCC or product company.
